\begin{proof}
  \uses{lem:flat_locus_open, def:stratum, def:stratum_immersion,
    thm:mem_range_stratum, thm:map_strata_ideal_basic_open}
  By the case \(n = 0\) of the flattening stratification
  (\cref{lem:flat_locus_open}), with its canonical scheme structure: locally
  on \(S\), a basis of \(\F \otimes \kappa(s)\) prolongs by Nakayama to a
  right-exact presentation
  \(\OO_V^{\oplus m} \xrightarrow{\psi} \OO_V^{\oplus e} \to \F|_V \to 0\)
  on a neighbourhood \(V\) of \(s\), and the closed subscheme
  \(V_e \subseteq V\) cut out by the ideal of matrix entries of \(\psi\)
  represents the locus where \(\F\) becomes locally free of rank \(e\):
  for \(f : T \to V\) the pulled-back presentation stays right-exact, so
  \(f^*\F\) is locally free of rank \(e\) if and only if \(f^*\psi = 0\),
  if and only if \(f\) factors through \(V_e\).  The local strata glue by
  this representing property into locally-closed subschemes
  \(S_e \subseteq S\) with \(|S_e|\) the rank-\(e\) locus; the family is
  finite because the fibre rank of a coherent module is bounded on a
  noetherian scheme, and the images are disjoint and cover \(|S|\) since
  every point has a well-defined fibre rank.

  For the universal property, let \(\varphi : T \to S\) have
  \(\varphi^*\F\) flat over \(T\).  A finitely presented flat module is
  locally free, and its rank is locally constant, so \(T\) decomposes into
  clopen pieces \(T_e\) on which \(\varphi^*\F\) is locally free of
  constant rank \(e\); by the representing property each restriction
  \(\varphi|_{T_e}\) factors uniquely through \(S_e\), and the
  factorizations assemble to \(\varphi = i \circ \tilde\varphi\) with
  \(\tilde\varphi : T \to \coprod_e S_e\).  Uniqueness: the strata have
  disjoint images, so any factorization through \(i\) induces the same
  decomposition of \(T\) into clopen preimages, and on each piece the
  component through \(S_e\) is unique because \(\iota_e\) is an immersion,
  hence a monomorphism.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  \uses{lem:point_rank_bounded, def:rank_stratum, def:rank_stratum_immersion,
    thm:mem_range_rank_stratum, thm:rank_stratum_flattens,
    lem:sheaf_flat_pullback, thm:rank_fibers_open, thm:point_rank_pullback,
    thm:factor_rank_stratum_unique, def:point_rank}
  \textbf{The strata.}  By \cref{lem:point_rank_bounded} there is an \(N\)
  bounding the point rank of \(\F\) on \(S\).  Take
  \(I := \{0, 1, \dots, N\}\) and, for \(e \in I\), the rank-\(e\) stratum
  \(\iota_e : S_e \to S\)
  (\cref{def:rank_stratum,def:rank_stratum_immersion}); each \(\iota_e\) is
  an immersion.  By \cref{thm:mem_range_rank_stratum} the image of
  \(\iota_e\) is exactly the locus of point rank \(e\); every point of
  \(S\) has a point rank, which is at most \(N\), so the images cover
  \(|S|\), and they are pairwise disjoint because the point rank is a
  single natural number.  Flatness of \(\iota_e^*\F\) over \(S_e\) is
  \cref{thm:rank_stratum_flattens}.

  \textbf{Factorization.}  Let \(\varphi : T \to S\) have \(\varphi^*\F\)
  flat over \(T\).  For \(e \in I\) let \(T_e \subseteq T\) be the locus
  where the point rank of \(\varphi^*\F\) equals \(e\).  By
  \cref{thm:point_rank_pullback} the point rank of \(\varphi^*\F\) at \(t\)
  is the point rank of \(\F\) at \(\varphi(t)\), hence at most \(N\); so
  the \(T_e\) cover \(T\), they are pairwise disjoint, and each is open by
  \cref{thm:rank_fibers_open}.  Thus \(T\) is the disjoint union of the
  open subschemes \(T_e\), and a morphism out of \(T\) is the same as a
  family of morphisms out of the \(T_e\).

  On a piece, the composite
  \(T_e \hookrightarrow T \xrightarrow{\varphi} S\) has flat pullback of
  \(\F\) --- it is the restriction of \(\varphi^*\F\) to the open subscheme
  \(T_e\), flat by \cref{lem:sheaf_flat_pullback} --- and, by
  \cref{thm:point_rank_pullback} again, the point rank of \(\F\) at the
  image of any \(t \in T_e\) is \(e\).  By
  \cref{thm:factor_rank_stratum_unique} there is a unique
  \(l_e : T_e \to S_e\) with \(\iota_e \circ l_e = \varphi|_{T_e}\).
  Define \(\psi : T \to \coprod_{f \in I} S_f\) on \(T_e\) as \(l_e\)
  followed by the coprojection of \(S_e\); then \(i \circ \psi = \varphi\),
  because this holds on each piece of the cover.

  \textbf{Uniqueness.}  Let \(\psi' : T \to \coprod_f S_f\) also satisfy
  \(i \circ \psi' = \varphi\).  Fix \(e\) and \(t \in T_e\), and let
  \(e'\) be the index of the summand containing \(\psi'(t)\), say
  \(\psi'(t) = z \in S_{e'}\).  Then
  \(\varphi(t) = i(\psi'(t)) = \iota_{e'}(z)\) lies in the image of
  \(\iota_{e'}\), so the point rank of \(\F\) at \(\varphi(t)\) is \(e'\)
  (\cref{thm:mem_range_rank_stratum}); it is also \(e\), since
  \(t \in T_e\) (\cref{thm:point_rank_pullback}).  Hence \(e' = e\): the
  morphism \(\psi'\) maps \(T_e\) into the open summand \(S_e\) of the
  coproduct, so \(\psi'|_{T_e}\) factors through the coprojection of
  \(S_e\) as some \(l'_e : T_e \to S_e\), and
  \(\iota_e \circ l'_e = i \circ \psi'|_{T_e} = \varphi|_{T_e}\).  The
  uniqueness in \cref{thm:factor_rank_stratum_unique} forces
  \(l'_e = l_e\); therefore \(\psi'\) and \(\psi\) agree on every piece
  \(T_e\), and \(\psi' = \psi\).
\end{proof}

1	---
2	name: blueprint-conventions
3	description: The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
4	---
5	
6	Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
7	Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.
8	
9	## Environments
10	
11	Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
12	`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
13	`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
14	its following `proof` environment form one node's content.
15	
16	## Per-node macros
17	
18	- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
19	- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration this node formalizes. Keep it 1-to-1: one
20	  blueprint node ↔ one Lean declaration, signatures matching.
21	- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
22	  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
23	  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
24	  proof.
25	- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
26	  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
27	  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
28	- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
29	  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
30	  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
31	- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
32	  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).
33	
34	## House style
35	
36	- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
37	  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
38	  and no conversational filler. If a Lean helper exists with no math counterpart,
39	  write its LaTeX statement so the 1-to-1 correspondence holds.
40	- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
41	  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
42	  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
43	  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
44	  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
45	  its proof stays complete.
46	- **One declaration's worth per node.** Don't restate Lean source as prose.
47	- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
48	  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
49	  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
50	  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

4	---
5	
6	The DAG links blueprint nodes by `\uses` edges. An edge `source -> target` means
7	*target depends on source*. The engine records each node's `\lean` link,
8	`proved`/`leanok` status, effort metrics, and Lean source metadata.
9	
10	## Keep It Fresh
11	
12	- Run the project build after Lean/blueprint edits so generated Lean artifacts and
13	  imported libraries are current.
14	- Run `horizon blueprint` after blueprint or Lean declaration changes; it writes
15	  `.archon-horizon/blueprints/<project>.json` for the dashboard and cached DAG
16	  consumers.
17	- Use `horizon leandag` for live inspection when deciding what to prove next.
18	
19	## `horizon leandag` (preferred)
20	
21	- `horizon leandag` — per-project summary: nodes, edges, proved count, and any
22	  isolated nodes (no edge in or out — usually a blueprint bug to fix).
23	- `horizon leandag -p <project> --node <label>` — one node's direct deps, full
24	  transitive cone, and reverse deps.
25	- `horizon leandag -p a -p b --union` — merge projects by declaration/node id.
26	  Same-id nodes are combined; divergent non-signature metadata is tolerated, but
27	  a Lean signature mismatch is an error to investigate.
28	- `horizon leandag -p a -p b --intersect` — only shared declaration/node ids,
29	  with the same signature check.
30	- Add `--json` for machine-readable output.
31	
32	A node is "ready" when all dependencies are proved. Prefer ready nodes when
33	choosing what to attempt next.
34	
35	## Cached JSON
36	
37	`horizon blueprint` writes each project's DAG to
38	`.archon-horizon/blueprints/<project>.json` (`nodes`, `edges`, `dangling`) for
39	the dashboard. Under the leandag engine, `\uses` are resolved at build/cache
40	time, so `dangling` is empty there; the parser fallback still populates it. To
41	check for orphan/unresolved nodes, use `horizon leandag` rather than relying only
42	on `dangling`.
